decision.scopeOfAccept: ACCEPT of doctor-fc-postreport-input-corpus.v1 as a DESIGN-CONTRACT-CANDIDATE at 0 blockers, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no express reservation. The artifact remains CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, and carries DO-NOT-SEAL on its own terms. It names four consented-invocation observation pairs and authors no consent-record bytes, no observations, and no envelope; OBL-DOCTOR-FX-AUTHORING is not closed and DR-114 is not SATISFIED.
decision.summaryForCoordinator: The envelope prohibition is the one with teeth here, so I tested it by probing rather than by reading the artifact's disclaimer. Live v4's FC-POSTREPORT passProperty enumerates the consent record's seven members — scope, endpoint, bytes, authorization, execution, result, and a non-null residual limitation — and I counted each name in the subject's bytes. Six occur ZERO times. The seventh, 'residual', occurs three times and every occurrence is a negation. No residualLimitation field exists, the adjacent failsIf vocabulary is absent too ('enforced' 0, 'confinement' 0, 'byte count' 0, 'schema' 0), and the four states carry exactly six field names between them with no nested object anywhere — structurally there is no envelope present to have been invented. The reason it is clean is worth naming: the subject declines to carry v4's passProperty at all, and since that is precisely where the seven-member envelope is written down, the omission is load-bearing rather than merely conservative. The scoping attack fails at the token level. v4 scopes the class to 'each pinned CONSENTED invocation', and the words that a denied or absent-consent state would need are simply not in the file — 'denied' 0, 'absent' 0, 'refused' 0, 'timed out' 0, 'failed' 0. I read the pinned sibling's live bytes to be sure what was being excluded: FC-CONSENT has exactly seven states, four consented and three not, and the subject's four map one-to-one onto the consented four while none of the other three appears. I also pressed the converse — that a failed or timed-out consented action should have been a fifth state — and it fails, because that case sits in v4's failsIf as a verdict condition, not in the exactByteIntent that enumerates the inputs. The pair mapping is exact: CA-1 and CA-2 share process-trace, CA-3 takes touched-resource-list, CA-4 takes network-capture, which is v4's clause verbatim including the fact that two classes share one observation form. The single quoted field is character-for-character equal to live. Custody is clean: subject unmoved at 56600056 and 0444 at both samplings, five of five cited digests equal live bytes, both cited standings opened and confirmed at Claude ACCEPT 0/0 with no Codex verdict, the D-164 join confirms OBL-DOCTOR-FX-AUTHORING still leftoverDesign true with owner none and FC-POSTREPORT inside its twelve, the thirteen-join-fixture count is right, HEAD 5d5d778, required-now 26, thirty gate rows, bare integers only 0/1/26, no control bytes, and SATISFIED and QUALIFIED occur zero times. Twenty attacks run, twenty refuted, zero findings. Two things for you. This artifact has NO annotation that time can falsify — the g12v2 role makes no recency claim, and the fcConsentV1 role makes no review-standing claim at all, only a structural one about seven states that I verified exactly. That is a better solution to the staleness problem than either dropping the clause (FC-D9) or naming both G12 versions (FC-REDACT), because it removes the surface rather than maintaining it. The one nit is that no evidence member is named, and this is the class where that costs most: FC-POSTREPORT is the only class in the family supplied at TWO members of the pinned G12 v2 — EV-4 'probe consent' and EV-6 'audit' — so a reader of this file alone cannot learn it carries two gate members rather than one.
